newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen mixed to slightly off at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen mixed to slightly off at open.

text.p: U.S. stocks were expected to open mixed to slightly lower on Tuesday, with some blue chips feeling pressure because of a higher interest rate environment but with technology stocks displaying strength.
The stock market could then work its way higher, if smaller-capitalization and tech shares had enough momentum to bolster the broader stock market, analysts said.

"The market could be off a little at the open," Michael Metz, chief investment strategist at Oppenheimer & Co, said. "The valuation of some big consumer durable goods stocks could be hurt by an uptick in rates."
But technology and smaller-capitalization stocks, which registered gains on Monday despite a weak bond market, could provide upward leadership.
"The shift into small-cap stocks is no longer subtle," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co, said.
Markets will also digest leading indicators for June, due at 1000 EDT/1400 GMT. They were forecast to rise 0.1 percent compared with a 0.3 percent gain in May.
In early trade, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures index was off 1.10 points at 945.30. The long bond was off lows but down 2/32 to yield 6.48 percent.
